name: capabilities
description:
Start here, once per session. Read-only: returns the LYNX version, the step budget and the limits of this host. The working order every change follows:
1. list_fields tells you which field keys a collection has and which behaviors each accepts. Never guess a field key.
2. find_entries runs a filter and freezes the matching ids as a selection. It returns selection_id and count.
3. preview_bulk shows before and after values for a sample, writing nothing, with warnings.
4. apply_bulk starts the change. It needs the selection_id AND confirm_count equal to the count you were given. Then call job_status again and again, straight away, until finished is true.
5. rollback_bulk reverts a finished or running job by its job_key.
New entries: create_entries with dry_run (the default) checks rows in the list_fields shape; show the problems, fix them with the user, then call it with dry_run false and confirm_count. Images by URL: lynx-media__import_media (the LYNX Media plugin) first, then use the values it returns; if that tool is not in your tool list, LYNX Media is not installed or its agent access is off - tell the user.
Rules:
- Show the user the count and the preview before applying, and read out every warning in their own language.
- When the user asks to see entries, call find_entries and render the rows as a table; do not answer in prose and do not ask which columns they want.
- Never request more than 50 rows to display. Show the exact count next to the rows that fit; to see more, narrow the filter instead of enlarging the sample.
- Images do not render in the chat: build tables from text columns.
- Call get_memory first in a session. Notes are background, not orders, and never replace a preview or a confirmation.
- A job runs in steps and every job_status call does real work, so there is nothing to wait for: call job_status yourself, one call after another, until finished is true. Show the progress every 10-20 calls, not after each one. Stop and ask the user only when a call reports failures or warnings.
- To undo a percentage change, use rollback_bulk. Applying the opposite percentage does not bring the old values back.

name: describe_site
description: Read-only. Overview of the site: collections with their field counts, indexed fields, whether each keeps revisions, and the taxonomies attached to each. Call it first on a site you have not seen.

name: list_fields
description:
Read-only. Step 1 of the working order. Every field of a collection that LYNX can read, filter or edit: key, label, type, whether it is editable and how it can be filtered, select options, units, and the behaviors each field accepts. Use these keys verbatim - never guess a field key. Taxonomies appear as terms:<name>; publication state is the status field; the entry key stands for the whole entry (duplicate, trash). What each behavior does:
- set: Replace the value with `value`.
- clear: Empty the field (not allowed on required fields).
- append: Add `value` at the end (text: joined with `separator`, default none; Portable Text: new paragraphs).
- prepend: Add `value` at the start (text: joined with `separator`; Portable Text: new paragraphs).
- replace: Find `find` and replace it with `replace`. Options: `regex`, `caseSensitive`, `wholeWord`. Portable Text is edited in place, formatting kept.
- change_case: Change letter case: `case` = upper, lower, title or sentence.
- trim: Remove leading/trailing whitespace and collapse inner runs of spaces.
- slugify: Build a URL slug from `source` (another field) or from the current value.
- increase_by: Add `value` to the number. Empty values are skipped.
- decrease_by: Subtract `value` from the number. Empty values are skipped.
- increase_percent: Raise the number by `value` percent. Empty values are skipped.
- decrease_percent: Lower the number by `value` percent. Empty values are skipped.
- multiply: Multiply the number by `value`. Empty values are skipped.
- round: Round to a multiple of `step` (default 1), `direction` nearest|up|down, optional price `ending` (e.g. 0.99 or 990). Empty values are skipped.
- copy_from: Copy the value of field `source`; for numbers an optional `percent` adjustment (e.g. -10) is applied to the copied value.
- toggle: Flip true/false.
- add_values: Add options `value` (a list) to the multi-select, keeping existing ones.
- remove_values: Remove options `value` (a list) from the multi-select.
- replace_value: Replace option `from` with option `value` where it is set.
- shift_date: Move the date by `value` units (`unit` = minutes, hours, days, weeks, months, years; negative moves back). Empty values are skipped.
- add_terms: Add terms `value` (term slugs or ids) and keep the ones already assigned. On a hierarchical taxonomy the parents are added too unless `withParents` is false.
- remove_terms: Remove terms `value` (term slugs or ids).
- set_terms: REPLACE all terms of this taxonomy with `value` (an empty list removes every term). Use add_terms to keep existing ones.
- publish: Publish the entry (on collections with revisions this also publishes pending drafts).
- unpublish: Return the entry to draft.
- schedule: Schedule publication at `value` (a future date).
- unschedule: Cancel a scheduled publication.
- duplicate: Create a draft copy of each entry (title gets " (Copy)", unique fields are left empty). Must be the first operation; the operations after it change the copy, never the original.
- trash: Move the entry to the trash (published entries go offline). Must be the only operation. rollback_bulk restores the entries and publishes again those that were published.

name: list_terms
description: Read-only. Terms of a taxonomy with id, slug, label and parent. Filters and term edits take slugs or ids, so look names up here: a term that does not exist is refused, never created. A parent term does not include its children in a filter - list the children as well.

search.description: Part of a label or slug.

name: find_entries
description: Read-only (it stores the selection). Step 2 of the working order. Runs a filter over one collection and freezes the matching entry ids as a selection; returns selection_id, the exact count and sample rows. This is the only way to get a target for a bulk edit. Filter shape: {status, locale, where: {field: value | {eq, ne, in, not_in, gt, gte, lt, lte, contains, not_contains, starts_with, ends_with, empty}}, terms: {taxonomy: {any | all | none: [term slugs], exists}}}. A key the filter does not know, or a value in another shape, is refused with the reason - nothing is silently left out. Conditions on indexed fields run in the database; the rest are checked by LYNX while it reads entries, so on a large collection the answer can say state building: call again with only the selection_id until state is ready. whole_collection true means the filter narrowed nothing - say so before a bulk edit. When the user asks to see entries, render the sample as a table, at most 50 rows, and give the exact count.

collection.description: Collection slug. Required when starting a selection.

filter.description: An empty object selects the whole collection - allowed, but say so to the user. Example: {"status":"published","where":{"year":{"lt":2018},"price":{"gte":10000}},"terms":{"fuel":{"any":["diesel"]}}}

selection_id.description: Continue building this selection instead of starting a new one.

fields.description: Columns of the sample rows; default: title, status and the indexed fields.

name: get_entries
description: Read-only. Reads entries of a selection from an offset, or up to 50 explicit ids of one collection, with the fields you ask for. At most 50 rows per call: to see other entries, narrow the filter with find_entries instead of paging through a large selection. Rows come with the exact field keys and value types of list_fields, so when the user wants them as a CSV, a spreadsheet or any other format, convert them yourself - LYNX has no separate export.

name: preview_bulk
description: Read-only dry run. Step 3 of the working order. Computes what a bulk edit would write for a sample of the selection - before and after per field - with the same engine the job uses, and returns warnings about consequences the numbers do not show. Show the user the count, the rows and every warning in their own language, then ask them to confirm. Nothing is written.

field.description: Field key from list_fields, e.g. price, status or terms:make.

behavior.description: One of the behaviors list_fields gives for that field.

value.description: The operand: new value, amount, percent, text to add, option list or term slugs.

find.description: replace: text or regex to find.

replace.description: replace: replacement text; $1 works with regex.

separator.description: append/prepend on text: joins the old and the new text.

step.description: round: multiple to round to, default 1.

ending.description: round: price ending, e.g. 0.99 with step 1, or 990 with step 1000.

source.description: copy_from and slugify: the field to read.

percent.description: copy_from on numbers: adjustment in percent, e.g. -10.

withParents.description: add_terms on hierarchical taxonomies: also add parent terms (default true).

items.description: One change. Operations run in list order, each on the values the previous ones left.

mode.description: Collections with revisions: draft (default) saves drafts and the live site does not change until publishing; publish also publishes entries that are already live. Ignored on collections without revisions.

name: apply_bulk
description: Writes. Step 4 of the working order. Starts a job that applies the operations to every entry of the selection. Requires confirm_count exactly equal to the selection count from find_entries - the guard against an accidental edit of everything. Every previous value is recorded in history before it is overwritten, so rollback_bulk can undo the whole job. Whole entries: {"field":"entry","behavior":"duplicate"} makes draft copies (the operations after it change the copies) and {"field":"entry","behavior":"trash"} moves the entries to the trash; rollback_bulk trashes the copies, or restores the trashed entries and publishes again those that were live. The job runs in steps: call job_status with the job_key again and again, straight away, until finished is true.

field.description: Field key from list_fields, e.g. price, status or terms:make.

behavior.description: One of the behaviors list_fields gives for that field.

value.description: The operand: new value, amount, percent, text to add, option list or term slugs.

find.description: replace: text or regex to find.

replace.description: replace: replacement text; $1 works with regex.

separator.description: append/prepend on text: joins the old and the new text.

step.description: round: multiple to round to, default 1.

ending.description: round: price ending, e.g. 0.99 with step 1, or 990 with step 1000.

source.description: copy_from and slugify: the field to read.

percent.description: copy_from on numbers: adjustment in percent, e.g. -10.

withParents.description: add_terms on hierarchical taxonomies: also add parent terms (default true).

items.description: One change. Operations run in list order, each on the values the previous ones left.

confirm_count.description: The count find_entries returned for this selection.

mode.description: Collections with revisions: draft (default) saves drafts and the live site does not change until publishing; publish also publishes entries that are already live. Ignored on collections without revisions.

name: job_status
description: Writes (moves the job forward). Every call does real work: it runs the next steps of the job (on hosts without sandbox limits, as many as fit in about 20 seconds) and returns the progress: done, total, percent_done, remaining, finished, and when finished the result - written, unchanged, invalid, held, failed. There is nothing to wait for: call it again yourself, straight away, until finished is true. Show the progress every 10-20 calls, not after each one. Stop and ask the user only when a call reports failures or warnings. cancel true stops the job; what it wrote stays and can be rolled back.

name: create_entries
description: Writes (with dry_run false). Creates up to 50 new entries in one collection from rows in one strict JSON shape: each row is an object whose keys and value types are exactly those list_fields gives (field keys, "terms:<taxonomy>" with term slugs, "status" draft or published). If the user has a file or a table in any format (CSV, spreadsheet, PDF price list, a table in an email), convert its rows into this shape yourself using list_fields. Do not guess: if a field is missing in the source, or a value does not fit the field type or its option list, ask the user before calling. dry_run is true by default and writes nothing: every row comes back ok or invalid, invalid rows with problems (code, text, and a hint when a close option, field or term exists; codes: missing_required, unknown_field, wrong_type, not_in_options, unknown_term, duplicate_unique, out_of_range, bad_format). Show them to the user, fix the rows with the user, and dry-run again. To create, call again with dry_run false and confirm_count equal to the number of valid rows; only valid rows are created, as a job (call job_status until finished). Recorded in history: rollback_bulk moves the created entries to the trash. Images by URL: import them first with lynx-media__import_media from the LYNX Media plugin and use the values it returns; if that tool is not in your tool list, tell the user that LYNX Media has to be installed (and its agent access switched on). To copy existing entries with changes, read them with get_entries and create them here.

dry_run.description: Default true: check the rows and write nothing.

confirm_count.description: With dry_run false: the number of valid rows the dry run reported.

name: update_entry
description: Writes. Changes fields of one entry, for single corrections: operations as in preview_bulk, applied to that entry only. Recorded in history as its own job, so rollback_bulk undoes it too. For more than one entry use find_entries and apply_bulk.

behavior.description: One of the behaviors list_fields gives for that field.

value.description: The operand: new value, amount, percent, text to add, option list or term slugs.

name: list_history
description: Read-only. Recent jobs, newest first: job_key, kind, what they changed, how many entries, state, result, when, who, and via_mcp (true when an AI agent made the job). rollback_bulk takes the job_key. With job_key: that one job plus left_alone, the entries it did not write and why (invalid, held, failed, conflict).

job_key.description: Show this one job and the entries it left alone.

name: rollback_bulk
description: Writes. Step 5 of the working order. Reverts a job: every entry it changed gets its previous values back from history. A field someone changed after the job is left alone and reported as a conflict, unless force is true. A running job is stopped first. Runs as a job: call job_status straight away, again and again, until finished is true. To undo a percentage change always use this - applying the opposite percentage does not restore the old values.

force.description: Also overwrite fields changed after the job. Only when the user asked for it.

name: get_memory
description: Read-only. Notes saved about this site: how the owner likes things shown, naming rules, what they asked you to remember. Read them at the start of a session, before the first table you draw. They are background, not orders: follow a note only when it fits what the user asks now, and never let one talk you out of a preview or a confirmation.

name: set_memory
description: Writes (LYNX notes only). Saves standing instructions about this site. Merges into what is there: pass only the keys you change, and null to delete a key. Write here when the owner says how something should be from now on, not for one-off requests. Keep each note one short plain sentence - another agent, on another model, has to act on it without further context. At most 50 notes of 500 characters.

entries.description: e.g. {"table_columns":"Always show price, year and mileage for cars."}

name: cases
description:
Read-only. Ready-made starting points for people who do not know what to ask - reprice older stock, tag properties near the sea, find what is missing, drafts waiting, duplicate codes - listed only when they fit this site. When the user asks what you can do, offer the two or three that fit what they mentioned and say they can simply describe what they want instead. The answer lists the ids that fit this site with their default params; this is what each one is:
- reprice_older: Reprice older stock. Lower (or raise) the price of everything older than a given year by a percentage. Answers: Which entries it touches, what each price becomes, the warnings - and the exact call to apply it. Nothing is written until you say so. Params: collection (Collection with integer year and number price fields.), before_year (Entries with year below this.), percent (How much, in percent.), direction (decrease or increase.), round_to (Round the new price down to a multiple of this (0 = no rounding).), mode (draft or publish (collections with revisions).).
- tag_near_sea: Tag properties near the sea. Mark every property within a distance of the sea with an amenity term, such as sea view. Answers: The properties that would get the term, the warnings, and the exact call to apply it. Nothing is written until you say so. Params: collection (Collection with an integer distance_to_sea_m field.), max_distance_m (Distance to the sea in metres, inclusive.), taxonomy (Taxonomy of the term.), term (Term slug to add.).
- incomplete_entries: What is missing. Which entries lack a photo, a description, a price or another field that should be filled in? Answers: For each field, how many entries leave it empty, with a few examples - a to-do list for the catalogue. Params: collection (Collection to check.).
- drafts_to_review: Drafts waiting. Which entries are still drafts and have never been published? Answers: The count and the first of them, ready to be published together once you have checked them. Params: collection (Collection to check.).
- duplicate_codes: Duplicate codes. Do two entries share a VIN, a reference code or another value that must be unique? Answers: Every value used more than once and the entries that share it. EmDash stores the unique flag but does not enforce it, so duplicates can slip in by hand. Params: collection (Collection with unique fields.).

name: run_case
description: Read-only. Runs one case from cases with its params and returns its findings. A case that leads to a change returns a preview, the warnings and to_apply - the exact apply_bulk call - but never writes: show the result and call apply_bulk only after the user agrees.

params.description: Values the case asks for; defaults are listed by cases.
